To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.

[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Review of Seller's Draft Against Buyer Playbook — Project Kestrel

Before the substance, one framing point. The Seller's preamble asserts these terms are "standard market," were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "agreed," and "FINAL / not to be re-opened." Treat this as negotiating rhetoric, not fact. Nothing in our playbook records any such principal-level agreement, and several positions below require **written authority from Amelia Frost that has not been given**. We should not let a drafting preamble manufacture consent we never gave. I would say so explicitly in our mark-up.

Now the material departures.

---

## 1. General liability cap (Clause 12.1)
**Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000.** Our opening position is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The 20% figure is only a *conditional fallback* that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft — **none exists**. So the Seller has drafted straight to our floor without the precondition being met.
**Push back:** reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not concede 20% unless/until Amelia authorises it in writing.

## 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)
**Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, recover only the excess.** Our playbook: **de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.** Seller is 5x our de minimis, 5x our basket, *and* converts the basket from a first-dollar (tipping) basket into a true deductible/excess-only basket.
**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery once the basket is exceeded.

## 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3/13)
**Seller: 18 months general; and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** Our position is **24 months**; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's written approval (**none given**). Worse, the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" sweep-up is a trap designed to pull Fundamental/Title/Tax/Fraud into the short period by default.
**Push back:** 24 months general. Reject the sweep-up; limitations must be category-specific, with Fundamental/Title/Tax and fraud expressly carved to their own regimes.

## 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller: capacity and title subject to the same caps/time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."** This directly collides with our requirement for a **separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to surrender title protection.
**Push back:** reject. Separate fundamental/title regime — 100% cap, minimum six years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier.

## 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
This is the most dangerous structural move. Making these apply to *all* Claims of *any* nature silently overrides the fundamental/title/tax regimes **and would capture fraud**. Our playbook is absolute: **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance — to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it.**
**Push back:** insert an express, unwaivable fraud/wilful-concealment/deliberate-misconduct carve-out overriding every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause. Carve title/tax/fundamental into their own regimes.

## 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)
**Seller relies on whole-data-room + public-register deemed disclosure** ([1.1] discloses "every fact… contained or referred to in the indexed data room"; [1.2] adds Accounts, statutory registers, public records). Our playbook **rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure** and requires **specific, fair disclosure**. Note [1.4] also pre-emptively denies that anything is "legally required" — a disclaimer we should not accept as limiting warranties.
**Push back:** disclosure must be specific and fairly disclosed in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete blanket data-room/register deemed disclosure.

## 7. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)
**Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records."** This is exactly the **blanket buyer-knowledge/constructive-knowledge exclusion we delete**. "Discoverable" imputes constructive knowledge — far beyond actual knowledge.
**Push back:** delete. If any qualifier survives, limit to the actual knowledge of named buyer individuals; never extend to constructive/"discoverable" knowledge, and never let it bar title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

## 8. Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3)
Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — plainly material. **Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats consent as "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."** The Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied.** Our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion — not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.**
**Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent *with satisfied conditions* a Completion condition. Reject reasonable-endeavours/consent-on-delivery.

## 9. Riverlark (Clause 2/7)
**Seller: release "to be provided following Completion"** on a facility of ~AUD 3,200,000. Disclosure §3: not repaid, no discharge included. Our playbook: **current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given).
**Push back:** obtain current payout figure; repay directly from Completion funds; secure effective release of security at/before Completion. A post-completion mechanism is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia's approval.

## 10. Employee bonuses — DD-005 (Funds flow)
**Seller: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised in the funds flow."** Disclosure §5 confirms they are omitted and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs. Our playbook: **the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.** "Not itemised" is the silent-exclusion risk — if omitted, the economic burden can fall on the Company (and thus us) post-Completion.
**Push back:** either seller-fund the bonuses *and on-costs* (payroll tax, super) explicitly, or make them a clear funds-flow line item reducing proceeds. Confirm on-cost treatment in writing.

## 11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)
**Seller: indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment, "considered adequate."** Disclosure §4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 shown open but **not independently verified**; no receipt or assignment in the data room. Risk: without payment, **IP/materials may not have transferred** — exposure exceeds a single fee. Our playbook: **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.**
**Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover loss from failure of the SOW3 IP/materials to vest (title, re-procurement, third-party claims), preserving the cure-on-payment mechanism. Do not accept AUD 180,000 as the agreed/verified figure.

## 12. Export/privacy incident — DD-006 (Clause 4.6/Schedule 6)
**Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."** Disclosure §6: download link sent to an unintended external address, ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed, scope, or notification duty. Our playbook: **preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.** So we neither accept Seller's "not material" characterisation nor assert a breach.
**Push back:** add covenants to preserve all logs/evidence, complete the investigation, and provide updates to the Buyer; keep rights reserved. Do not let "preliminary/not material" prejudice later claims. Do not insert any numeric figure.

## 13. Sandbar renewals (Supplier renewals)
**Seller: three × AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs."** Disclosure §8 admits it is silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Our playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** So symmetrically we don't automatically accept "ordinary course" either.
**Push back:** seek the renewal documents to assess terminability/accrual. Do not accept blanket "ordinary course"; but we are not asserting automatic Debt/price deduction.

## 14. Title evidence (Clause / Disclosure §10)
**Seller: title evidenced solely by the DD-012 share register.** Our playbook: **require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.** Seller's own §10 concedes the Buyer hasn't verified.
**Push back:** require independent evidence of share ownership, encumbrances and authority (e.g. certified constitutional/register documents, officer certificates, ASIC searches, confirmation of no security interests/PPSR). An internal register alone is insufficient.

## 15. Tax / IP
**Seller: "settled under the general regime above."** Our playbook keeps **Tax and IP OPEN**, separate from the general regime, with **no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.** Folding them into the general cap/time regime is another silent override (same mechanism as item 5).
**Push back:** Tax and IP remain open and are not subsumed into the general regime. Keep categories separate.

## 16. Ancillary consents noted but lower priority
- **Office lease (DD-007, §7):** notification obligation, not stated to require landlord consent for a share sale. Confirm the trigger and whether notice is needed — monitor, not a dealbreaker.
- **Mossvale (DD-009, §9):** assignment restriction said not triggered by a share sale. Confirm change-of-control language doesn't bite; low priority on current facts.

---

## Summary of Recommendations
1. **Reject the "FINAL / already agreed" framing.** No principal-level agreement exists on our side; several Seller positions require Amelia Frost's written authority that has **not** been given (20% cap, 18-month period, any post-completion Riverlark release).
2. **Cap:** restore **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. 
3. **Thresholds:** **AUD 5,000** de minimis, **AUD 50,000** first-dollar basket.
4. **Time:** **24 months** general; delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep-up.
5. **Fundamental/Title/Tax:** **separate regime** — 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. Reject "administrative simplicity" merger and the "all Claims" override.
6. **Fraud carve-out:** insert an **express, unwaivable** carve-out of fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
7. **Disclosure:** specific/fair disclosure only; delete whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete the blanket/"discoverable" exclusion; at most actual knowledge of named individuals, never barring title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** effective consent **with satisfied conditions** as a Completion condition; reject reasonable-endeavours/consent-on-delivery.
10. **Riverlark:** payout figure + direct repayment from Completion funds + effective security release; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia's approval.
11. **DD-005 bonuses:** seller-fund or itemise **AUD 420,000 plus on-costs**; no silent exclusion.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity to cover IP/materials non-vesting, preserve SOW3 cure; don't treat AUD 180,000 as verified.
13. **DD-006 incident:** preserve-logs/investigate/update covenants, rights reserved; accept no "not material" characterisation and insert no numbers.
14. **Sandbar:** obtain documents to assess; reject blanket "ordinary course"; assert no automatic Debt/price deduction.
15. **Title:** require **independent** ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register alone insufficient.
16. **Tax/IP:** remain open; keep categories separate; no unlimited liability assumed.
17. **Monitor** office-lease notification and Mossvale change-of-control; confirm neither requires third-party consent for the share sale.

Two escalation flags for the deal team: items **2 (cap→20%)**, **3 (18-month period)** and **9 (post-completion Riverlark release)** all need **Amelia Frost's written sign-off** before we could ever concede them. I'd recommend we hold our opening positions and not treat any of these as live concessions in the next turn.

Want me to draft the mark-up/issues list in a format you can send back to Seller's counsel?
